claims.text: Replacing TOR-TILD's conventional EAM reference with an MLIP trained on both liquid and solid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed MLIP can be a Gaussian Approximation Potential or a neural-network potential.
The MLIP should be trained on ab initio data sampled from both liquid and solid configurations of the high-entropy alloy.
The intervention is applicable to equiatomic or near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
The applicable temperature interval extends from the melting point to slightly above it.
Isothermal and isobaric calculations will ensure that both solid and liquid states are sampled.
An MLIP trained on both phases will capture a broad spectrum of atomic configurations present in the solid and liquid.
Training on the diverse atomic arrangements of the ab initio liquid will allow the MLIP to represent local-environment variations more accurately than EAM.
More accurate representation of local environments will enhance overlap between the MLIP reference and ab initio target phase spaces.
Enhanced phase-space overlap will reduce the effective length and mismatch of the thermodynamic-integration path.
The MLIP reference will produce lower integration-path mismatch than TOR-TILD's EAM reference.
Free-energy differences obtained using the MLIP reference will be closer to direct ab initio benchmark values than those obtained using the EAM reference.
The approach may not extend to highly skewed alloy compositions.
The approach may not extend to conditions far from the melting regime.
